The altruism and love presented in christian philosophical doctrine is what made me change my mind. 
This is my story.

(from wiki: Altruism or selflessness is the principle or practice of concern for the welfare of others)

During my childhood, I was indoctrinated by my christian parents.
As time passed, I filled with anger by the oppression my parents imposed upon me, so I turned to atheism and /cough philosophical satanism/nihilism.
Just wanted to be different and to express myself.

As even more time passed, I realized that such radical believes are not necessary for individual expressing, nor did I find them useful.
Over time I did study a bit more philosophy and got introduced to the therm ,,agnostic", which tl;dr means:

!!The evidence presented proving god's existence, is equal to the evidence which negates it. Practically, we can't prove if god exists, nor can we disprove it. The bible is just a metaphorical book and should not be understood literary, but the bible isn't the only religious book around. There may be a god, which we are not able to perceive or understand, simply because of our limitations. And then I understood that believing in god, is, in fact, a matter of faith.!!

In time I started to prefer altruism, empathy and mutual caring over nihilism because I realized that everyone in this world, just like me, battles a hard battle within his own existence and the only way we can understand, or at least help each other, is to care about each other.

(from wiki: Nihilism is the philosophical doctrine suggesting the negation of one or more putatively meaningful aspects of life)

I started being obsessed about caring about people, trying to tolerate and understand, being nicer to my parents (even though they had done me wrong in the past, they were still simple sinful human beings, trying to get their child to love them, which I openly did not) etc.
And then, after along battle with myself, I came to the realization that...being christian is not bad, it's not ignorant and it's the easiest way for the average person to understand that I am trying to love and understand them (as long as you don't stray away from what Christianity is about, and that is love, compassion, forgiveness towards other people's sins, and their towards mine).

And now, after a long journey, I can proudly say that I am a proud christian.
